summary.text: A 57-year-old man had sudden-onset rotational vertigo and fever for 10 hours while at work. Emergency CT and MRI ruled out central pathology, and a pharyngeal swab confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection. The vertigo resolved but residual dizziness exacerbated by neck rotation persisted. His only significant history was a gastric ulcer, and he presented to the authors hospital two months later.

Enzyme immunoassay showed elevated herpes simplex virus-1 and varicella zoster virus IgG. Examination showed spontaneous left-beating nystagmus, normal pure-tone audiometry, absent right-ear caloric responses with significant canal paresis, reduced right lateral canal vHIT gain, normal cVEMP and reduced right oVEMP. These findings indicated right superior vestibular neuritis; head-up tilt showed instantaneous orthostatic hypotension.

He received antivertigo medication, adenosine triphosphate and vitamin B12 with vestibular rehabilitation exercises. At four and seven months he declined repeat caloric testing. oVEMP and Foulage results improved slightly by four months, and at seven months vHIT gain rose and oVEMP responses became nearly symmetrical, while sway testing showed persistently impaired dynamic stability.

Dizziness handicap scores reflected reduced dizziness and HADS scores were within normal range. Head-up tilt testing suggested persistent autonomic dysfunction and left cVEMP p13 latency was prolonged, suggesting sacculo-collic reflex impairment. Improvements in vHIT and oVEMP were consistent with vestibular neuritis recovery, with persistent postural instability, and continued follow-up is planned.

caption_evidence.quote:
Figure 2
Course of posturography and Foulage test(A) Temporal changes in the center of pressure during static posturography. The four center of pressure diagrams for each condition are as follows: the upper left shows standing with eyes open; the upper right shows standing with eyes closed; the lower left shows standing with eyes open with a rubber load; and the lower right shows standing with eyes closed with a rubber load. The Y-axis represents front-back movement, and the X-axis represents left-right movement. Rubber loading reduces somatosensory input, allowing vestibular, visual, and somatosensory-dependent elements to be evaluated. (B) Temporal changes in the Foulage test. The four statokinesigrams for each condition are as follows: the upper left shows the center of pressure during stepping with eyes open; the upper right shows the center of pressure during stepping with eyes closed; the lower left shows the variances of steps with eyes open; and the lower right shows the variances of steps with eyes closed. Red indicates the distribution of the right foot’s center of pressure at the time of landing, and blue indicates the distribution of the left foot’s center of pressure. The Y-axis shows front-back movement, and the X-axis shows left-right movement. The Foulage test assesses dynamic equilibrium and determines susceptibility to disturbances.
